title: How to Strum a Guitar WITHOUT a Pick
summary: JustinGuitar’s beginner-to-intermediate guide explores strumming on guitar without a pick, focusing on finger-style options, tonal variation, and practical patterns. The lesson covers why players might avoid a pick, contrasts fleshy-thumb tones with nail tones, and methodically demonstrates several approaches using the thumb or the first finger (alone or combined), including how to angle the hand to avoid strings catching, how much arm versus finger motion to use, and how to blend thumb and finger techniques for different song needs. It presents common patterns such as bass-notes on beats 1 and 3 with a down/up strum on 2 and 4, backbeat feel, and the concept of mixing strumming with fingerstyle to add melody and rhythm. The video emphasizes comfort, musical context, and the idea that there isn’t a single “right” method, encouraging self-observation, experimentation, and tailoring technique to the song and player level (with a nod toward more advanced, percussive fingerstyle later in the journey).
